verdicts.reasoning: The samples require the student to break down the given number into its constituent parts, either by expressing it as an addition equation separating the tens value and ones value (e.g., 40 + 5) or by constructing the number using base-10 blocks that separate the tens and ones.
Every sample explicitly uses a 2-digit number (e.g., 10, 20, 45, 50) as the target number to be decomposed or built.

The text-based questions explicitly ask the student to write the number 'as tens and ones' using expanded form (e.g., 40 + 5), and the visual questions use base-10 blocks with specific tens and ones quantities in the payload to represent the number.
